# Vandana (වන්දනා)

> Vandana is a free reader for Sinhala Buddhist pirith (paritta) chants and everyday worship verses (vandana gatha), with the full Pali text in Sinhala script.

Texts are in Pali or Sinhala, written in Sinhala script. Each link below is a page with the full text.
The complete text of every page is in one file: https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/llms-full.txt

## Pirith (පිරිත්)

Protective Buddhist chants (paritta), such as Jaya Piritha, Ratana Sutta and Karaniya Metta Sutta, in Sinhala script.

- [දසධම්ම සූත්‍රය (Dasadhamma Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/dasadhamma-suthraya): Ten things a monk should reflect on often.
- [මහා මංගල සූත්‍ර‍ය (Maha Mangala Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mahamangala-suthraya): The Buddha's discourse on the thirty-eight highest blessings in life.
- [රතන සූත්‍රය (Ratana Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/rathana-suthraya): The 'Jewel discourse', chanted to dispel famine, disease and fear in Vesali; one of the main protective suttas.
- [කරණීයමෙත්ත සූත්‍රය (Karaniya Metta Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/karaneeyameththa-suthraya): The discourse on loving-kindness towards all beings, chanted for protection and peace of mind.
- [ඛන්ධ පරිත්තය (Khandha Paritta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/khandha-piritha): Loving-kindness to all kinds of snakes and creatures, taught after a monk died of snakebite; chanted for protection.
- [මෙත්තානිසංස සූත්‍රය (Mettanisamsa Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/meththanisansa-suthraya): The eleven benefits of developing loving-kindness.
- [මිත්තානිසංස ගාථා (Mittanisamsa)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/miththanisansa-gatha): Verses on the blessings that come to one who is loyal to friends, from the Mugapakkha Jataka.
- [මෝර පරිත්තය (Mora Paritta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mora-piritha): The peacock's protection, recited morning and evening by the Bodhisatta as a golden peacock.
- [චන්ද පරිත්තය (Canda Paritta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/chanda-piritha): The moon deity, seized by Rahu, is set free when he goes for refuge to the Buddha.
- [සූරිය පරිත්තය (Suriya Paritta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/suriya-piritha): The sun deity, seized by Rahu, is set free when he goes for refuge to the Buddha.
- [ධජග්ග සූත්‍රය (Dhajagga Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/dhajagga-suthraya): The banner's crest: recollecting the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha to overcome fear.
- [මහාකස්සප බොජ්ඣංග සූත්‍රය (Maha Kassapa Bojjhanga Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mahakassapa-bojjanga-suthraya): The seven factors of awakening, taught to the ill Venerable Maha Kassapa, who recovered.
- [මහාමොග්ගල්ලාන බොජ්ඣංග සූත්‍රය (Maha Moggallana Bojjhanga Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mahamoggallana-bojjanga-suthraya): The seven factors of awakening, taught to the ill Venerable Maha Moggallana, who recovered.
- [මහාචුන්ද බොජ්ඣංග සූත්‍රය (Maha Cunda Bojjhanga Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mahachunda-bojjanga-suthraya): The seven factors of awakening, recited by Venerable Cunda when the Buddha himself was ill.
- [ගිරිමානන්‍ද සූත්‍රය (Girimananda Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/girimananda-suthraya): The ten perceptions taught for the ill Venerable Girimananda, traditionally chanted for the sick.
- [ඉසිගිලි සූත්‍රය (Isigili Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/isigili-suthraya): The names of the Paccekabuddhas who lived on Isigili mountain.
- [ධම්මචක්කපවත්තන සූත්‍රය (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/dhamma-chakka-pawattana-sutta): The Buddha's first sermon at Isipatana, which sets out the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path.
- [මහාසමය සූත්‍රය (Mahasamaya Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mahasamaya-suthraya): The great assembly of deities who gathered to see the Buddha and the Sangha.
- [ආළවක සූත්‍රය (Alavaka Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/alawaka-suthraya): The Buddha's answers to the questions of the yakkha Alavaka, who then became his follower.
- [කසීභාරද්වාජ සූත්‍රය (Kasi Bharadvaja Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/kasibharadwaja-suthraya): The Dhamma as ploughing, taught to the farming brahmin Kasi Bharadvaja.
- [පරාභව සූත්‍රය (Parabhava Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/parabhawa-suthraya): The causes of downfall in a person's life.
- [වසල සූත්‍රය (Vasala Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/wasala-suthraya): One becomes an outcast or a noble one by deeds, not by birth.
- [සච්චවිභඞ්ග සූත්‍රය (Saccavibhanga Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/sachchavibhanga-suthraya): A detailed analysis of the Four Noble Truths, given by Venerable Sariputta.
- [ආටානාටිය සූත්‍රය (Atanatiya Sutta)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/atanatiya-suthraya): A protection given by the Four Great Kings against harmful spirits.
- [බොජ්ඣංග පිරිත (Bojjhanga Piritha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/bojjanga-piritha): The seven factors of enlightenment (bojjhanga), traditionally chanted for people who are ill.
- [ජය පිරිත (Jaya Piritha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/jaya-piritha): Verses recalling the Buddha's virtues and victory, chanted for success, protection and blessings.
- [මහා ජයමංගල ගාථා (Maha Jaya Mangala Gatha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/mahajayamangala-gatha): Verses wishing victory and blessings, often chanted at the end of a pirith ceremony.
- [අටවිසි පිරිත (Atawisi Piritha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/atawisi-piritha): Verses recalling the names of the twenty-eight Buddhas, chanted for protection and blessings.
- [ඇනවුම් පිරිත (Anawum Piritha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/anawum-piritha): Verses chanted at the start of a pirith ceremony to invite the deities to come and listen.
- [ජින පඤ්ජරය (Jina Panjaraya)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/jinapanjaraya): The 'Buddha's cage': verses that place the Buddhas and great disciples around the body for protection.

## Daily worship (මූලික වන්දනාව)

Everyday Buddhist worship: homage to the Buddha, worship of the Triple Gem, offerings and sharing merit, in Sinhala script.

- [බුද්ධ පූජා ගාථා (Buddha Puja Gatha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/buddhapuja-ghatha): Verses for offering lamps, incense, flowers and food to the Buddha.
- [දෙවියන්ට පින්දීම (Merit sharing with the deities)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/deviyanta-pindeema): Verses for sharing the merit of a good deed with the deities and all beings (Ettavata ca amhehi).
- [නමස්කාරය හා බුද්ධ වන්දනා (Namaskaraya and Buddha Vandana)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/namaskaraya): The homage 'Namo tassa', taking the Triple Refuge, and verses for worshipping the Buddha.
- [සෙත් පැතීම (Seth Pathima)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/seth-pathima): Blessing verses wishing health, long life and freedom from danger (Sabbitiyo vivajjantu).
- [තෙරුවන් වන්දනාව (Theruwan Vandanawa)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/theruwan-vandanawa): Worship of the Triple Gem: verses recalling the qualities of the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha (Itipiso).
- [සරණගමනය (Saranagamana)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/saranagamanaya): Going for refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha, three times; recited at the start of every chanting.
- [දස සික්ඛාපද (Dasa Sikkhapada)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/dasa-sikkhapada): The ten training precepts undertaken by novice monks and by lay people on special days.
- [සාමණේර පඤ්හය (Samanera Panha)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/samanera-panhaya): The novice's questions: ten questions and answers on the Dhamma, from one to ten.
- [ද්වත්තිංසාකාරය (Dvattimsakara)](https://vandana.sudaraka94.com/articles/dvattimsakaraya): The thirty-two parts of the body, recited as a reflection on the body.
